theory.intro: A negative index means take the reciprocal of the base. When the base is a fraction, taking the reciprocal simply turns that fraction upside down and the index becomes positive. This gives a quick way to simplify any expression of the form $\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^{-n}$.
facts: $\left(\frac{a}{b}\right)^{-n}=\left(\frac{b}{a}\right)^{n}=\frac{b^{n}}{a^{n}}$ — invert first, then raise to the positive index.
Every factor inside the brackets is raised to the index, coefficients included: $\left(\frac{2x}{3}\right)^{-2}=\left(\frac{3}{2x}\right)^{2}=\frac{9}{4x^{2}}$.
A term with no denominator can be written over $1$, so $\left(\frac{4}{1}\right)^{-1}=\frac{1}{4}$.
The negative sign in the index never becomes a negative sign in the answer: $\left(\frac{3}{4}\right)^{-1}=\frac{4}{3}$, not $-\frac{4}{3}$.
steps: Simplify the fraction inside the brackets if it can be simplified.
Invert the fraction and change the index to positive.
Raise every factor in the numerator and the denominator to that index.
